chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn Abdillah from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, and Abu Talib al-Anbari narrated it, saying: Ahmad ibn Hawza Abu Bakr al-Hafiz narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hudhayni narrated to me, saying: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, saying: Al-Zuhri narrated to me from Ubaydillah ibn Abdillah ibn Utbah.

He said: I sat with Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), and the mention of fixed shares (al-fara'id) and inheritances was presented to him. Ibn Abbas said: Glory be to Allah the Great. Do you think that He who counted the grains of sand in 'Araj made in the estate half and half and a third, and these two halves have already taken the estate, so where is the place of the third?

Zufar ibn Aws al-Basri said to him: O Abu al-Abbas, who was the first to prioritize the fixed shares? He said: Umar ibn al-Khattab. When the fixed shares gathered at his side and one displaced the other, he said: By Allah, I do not know which of you Allah prioritized and which He delayed. I find nothing broader than that I distribute this estate to you in shares, and I will enter for every person with a right the right that entered him due to the 'awl (displacement) of the fixed share.

And by Allah, if He had prioritized who He prioritized and delayed who He delayed, no fixed share would have been displaced. Zufar ibn Aws said to him: So which did He prioritize and which did He delay?

He said: Every fixed share that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not demote from one fixed share to another, this is what Allah prioritized. As for what Allah delayed, every fixed share, when it is removed from its obligatory portion, has nothing left for it except what remains; those are the ones He delayed.

As for what Allah prioritized: The husband has half, but when something enters upon him that removes him from it, he returns to a quarter; nothing removes him from it except that. The wife has a quarter, but when it is removed from her, it becomes an eighth; nothing removes her from it except that. The mother has a third, but when it is removed from her, it becomes a sixth; nothing removes her from it except that. These are the fixed shares that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prioritized.

As for what Allah delayed: The fixed share of daughters and sisters, for her half and for her two-thirds. If the fixed shares remove them from that, she has nothing left except what remains; those are what Allah delayed.

So when what Allah prioritized and what He delayed come together, that which was prioritized is begun with, and its right is given in full. If something remains, it is for that which was delayed. If nothing remains, then she has nothing.
Zufar ibn Aws said to him: So what prevented you from suggesting this opinion to Umar? He said: I feared him.
Al-Zuhri said: By Allah, if it were not that an upright Imam preceded him, his matter would have been more decisive in piety. He said: Two people differed with Ibn Abbas regarding the issue.

key_terms.عَوْل: Displacement (of a share due to another heir)

ai.seo_question: How did Ibn Abbas explain Umar's method of resolving conflicting inheritance shares?
ai.summary: Ibn Abbas elucidates the jurisprudential rationale behind Umar ibn al-Khattab’s innovation of 'Aul' (proportional reduction) in inheritance distribution, distinguishing between 'prioritized' shares that retain a minimum entitlement and 'delayed' shares that are fully displaced. This method ensures that fixed portions like the husband’s half or mother’s third are secured before residual heirs receive their shares, a principle later adopted by the Sunni schools and highly regarded in Shia scholarship for its logical consistency. The narration highlights the transition from the Prophet’s era to the Caliphate, where Umar’s practical solution to conflicting shares was validated by Ibn Abbas’s theological justification.
